newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile rejects huge Norwegian fishing ship.
newsitem.headline: Chile rejects huge Norwegian fishing ship.

text.p: Chile refused on Thursday to allow a huge Norwegian trawler to operate in its southern Pacific waters after a campaign by ecologists who feared the ship would decimate dwindling fish stocks.

The government rejected an application by local fishing company Pesquera Yelcho to replace three smaller boats whose fishing licences had expired with the Norwegian-built factory ship American Monarch, said Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia.
"The foreign investment committee, in a session presided over by the economy minster, rejected the proposal made by Pesquera Yelcho," Garcia said in a statement.
American Monarch, the world's largest factory boat, can process up to 1,000 tonnes of fish a day and was expected to work in rich fishing grounds close to Chile's southern tip.

Greenpeace, which led the campaign against the ship, said the committee's decision would help traditional fishermen who have complained that their fishing areas are being over-exploited by a growing number of industrial boats.
"We and Chile's traditional fisherman take the news as a partial victory," said Juan Carlos Cardenas, who headed Greenpeace's campaign against the American Monarch.
